metadata.scenario: A customer calls questioning a recent charge that does not match their service agreement. Category: Billing. Flags: billing_dispute.

transcription.text: Thank you for calling CareFirst Home Health, this is Margaret speaking. How can I assist you today? Hi, Margaret. My name is Thomas White, and I'm calling about a recent charge on my account that I don't understand. I'm sorry to hear that, Thomas. Let's take a look at your account. Can I have your account number, please? Sure, it's 3456789. The charge was for $300, but I was expecting a different amount for the dementia care services. Thank you for that information. I’ll pull up your account now. Just a moment, please. Alright, I see your account here. It looks like there was a charge for 24/7 live-in care instead of the respite services you initially requested. That’s exactly it! I specifically agreed to respite care, as I need help for just a few hours a day. I understand your concern, Thomas. Let me clarify that for you. The live-in care is much more intensive. Yes, I realize that. It’s not what I signed up for, and the price difference is significant. I apologize for the confusion. It seems there was a miscommunication regarding your service schedule. I’d like to resolve this today if possible. Can you help me correct the billing issue? Absolutely. I can initiate a billing dispute for this charge. I will also adjust your service back to the respite care you need. That sounds good. What happens next? I will file the dispute within our system, and you should see a refund for the difference within 5-7 business days. Thank you, I appreciate that. Will I receive any confirmation? Yes, you will receive an email confirmation once the dispute is filed and processed. Great! And I’d also like to discuss starting respite care for my mother. Of course! Our respite care services are $30 to $38 per hour. How many hours per week are you looking for? I think around 20 hours a week would be good. Perfect! I can set that up for you. Would you like me to connect you with Lisa Chen, our Care Coordinator? Yes, please. That would be great to get everything arranged. Alright, I’ll transfer you to Lisa now. She can assist with the care plan development and scheduling. Thank you, Margaret. I appreciate your help. You’re welcome, Thomas. Enjoy your day, and hold on a moment while I connect you. (transferring call) (transferring) (transferring)
